requirements.text: When the user clicks any visible piano key on the webpage, identified by its data-testid (e.g., 'piano-key-a' for the white key 'a' or 'piano-key-w' for the black key 'w'), the system must play the corresponding sound file from the 'tunes' directory (e.g., 'tunes/a.wav' for key 'a'). The clicked key must receive the 'active' class to visually highlight it, and the highlight must be removed after 150ms by removing the 'active' class.

The system must allow the user to adjust the audio volume using a slider (data-testid='volume-slider') with a range from 0 (mute) to 1 (maximum volume). Interacting with the slider updates the audio volume accordingly, with 0 muting the audio, 1 playing at full volume. The volume change must be reflected immediately upon slider adjustment.

When the user interacts with the 'Show Keys' checkbox (identified by `data-testid='show-keys-checkbox'`), the system must toggle the visibility of key labels on the piano keys (identified by `data-testid` starting with 'piano-key') by adding or removing the 'hide' class. Initially, the labels are visible. When the checkbox is checked, clicking it should hide the labels by adding the 'hide' class to all piano keys. When unchecked, clicking it should restore the labels by removing the 'hide' class. The system must handle rapid toggling, ensuring the final state of the labels is consistent and correct.

The system must display all piano keys (white and black) in the UI, each labeled with its corresponding keyboard key. The piano keys must include both white and black keys, with the following labels: 'a', 'w', 's', 'e', 'd', 'f', 't', 'g', 'y', 'h', 'u', 'j', 'k', 'o', 'l', 'p', ';'. Each key must be represented as an HTML <li> element with the class 'key' and either 'white' or 'black', depending on the type of key. The keys must also include a 'data-key' attribute corresponding to their label and a 'data-testid' attribute in the format 'piano-key-{label}' (e.g., 'piano-key-a'). The labels must be displayed as <span> elements nested within the <li> elements. The keys must be contained within a <ul> element with the class 'piano-keys'. The system must ensure that all keys are visible by default when the webpage is loaded, and their labels must be displayed unless the 'Show Keys' checkbox is unchecked. The checkbox must be represented as an HTML <input> element with the type 'checkbox', a 'data-testid' attribute of 'show-keys-checkbox', and must toggle the visibility of the labels when clicked.
The system must allow users to interact with the piano keys using both mouse clicks and keyboard presses, ensuring consistent functionality across both input methods.

reference_cases.title: [Normal] User clicks on a white piano key
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Play piano sound and visually highlight the key when clicked
  The system must play the corresponding piano sound and visually highlight the key when the user clicks on a piano key. The highlight should disappear after 150ms.


Scenario: [Normal] User clicks on a white piano key
    Given the webpage is loaded and the piano keys are visible
    When the user clicks on the white piano key with data-testid "piano-key-a"
    Then the system must play the sound 
    And the key with data-testid "piano-key-a" must have the "active" class added
    And the "active" class must be removed from the key with data-testid "piano-key-a" after 150ms

    And the "active" class must be removed from the key with data-testid "piano-key-w" after 150ms

reference_cases.title: [Edge] User clicks multiple piano keys in quick succession
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Play piano sound and visually highlight the key when clicked
  The system must play the corresponding piano sound and visually highlight the key when the user clicks on a piano key. The highlight should disappear after 150ms.


Scenario: [Edge] User clicks multiple piano keys in quick succession
    Given the webpage is loaded and the piano keys are visible
    When the user clicks on the white piano key with data-testid "piano-key-a"
    And immediately clicks on the black piano key with data-testid "piano-key-w"
    Then the system must play the sound
    And the system must play the sound
    And the key with data-testid "piano-key-a" must have the "active" class added
    And the key with data-testid "piano-key-w" must have the "active" class added
    And the "active" class must be removed from the key with data-testid "piano-key-a" after 150ms
    And the "active" class must be removed from the key with data-testid "piano-key-w" after 150ms

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Adjusting the volume slider updates the audio playback volume
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Adjusting the volume slider to control audio playback volume
  The user should be able to adjust the volume slider to control the audio playback volume, with values ranging from 0 (mute) to 1 (maximum volume).


  Scenario: [Normal] Adjusting the volume slider updates the audio playback volume
    Given the piano webpage is loaded
    And the volume slider with data-testid "volume-slider" is visible and set to 0.5
    When the user moves the volume slider to 0.8
    Then the audio playback volume should be updated to 0.8

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Setting the volume slider to the minimum value (mute)
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Adjusting the volume slider to control audio playback volume
  The user should be able to adjust the volume slider to control the audio playback volume, with values ranging from 0 (mute) to 1 (maximum volume).


  Scenario: [Edge] Setting the volume slider to the minimum value (mute)
    Given the piano webpage is loaded
    And the volume slider with data-testid "volume-slider" is visible and set to 0.5
    When the user moves the volume slider to 0
    Then the audio playback volume should be updated to 0

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Setting the volume slider to the maximum value
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Adjusting the volume slider to control audio playback volume

reference_cases.title: [Error] Providing an invalid value outside the slider range
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Adjusting the volume slider to control audio playback volume
  The user should be able to adjust the volume slider to control the audio playback volume, with values ranging from 0 (mute) to 1 (maximum volume).


  Scenario: [Error] Providing an invalid value outside the slider range
    Given the piano webpage is loaded
    And the volume slider with data-testid "volume-slider" is visible and set to 0.5
    When the user attempts to set the volume slider to -0.5
    Then the audio playback volume should remain unchanged at 0

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Toggle key labels visibility on checkbox click
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Toggle visibility of piano key labels
  The system must toggle the visibility of the key labels on the piano keys when the user clicks the 'Show Keys' checkbox.


  Scenario: [Normal] Toggle key labels visibility on checkbox click
    Given the Playable Piano page is loaded
    And the 'Show Keys' checkbox with data-testid 'show-keys-checkbox' is checked
    When the user clicks the 'Show Keys' checkbox
    Then each piano key with data-testid starting with 'piano-key' should have the 'hide' class added

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Restore key labels visibility on checkbox click
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Toggle visibility of piano key labels
  The system must toggle the visibility of the key labels on the piano keys when the user clicks the 'Show Keys' checkbox.


  Scenario: [Normal] Restore key labels visibility on checkbox click
    Given the Playable Piano page is loaded
    And the 'Show Keys' checkbox with data-testid 'show-keys-checkbox' is unchecked
    When the user clicks the 'Show Keys' checkbox
    Then each piano key with data-testid starting with 'piano-key' should have the 'hide' class removed

reference_cases.title: [Edge] Rapid toggling of the 'Show Keys' checkbox
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Toggle visibility of piano key labels
  The system must toggle the visibility of the key labels on the piano keys when the user clicks the 'Show Keys' checkbox.


  Scenario: [Edge] Rapid toggling of the 'Show Keys' checkbox
    Given the Playable Piano page is loaded
    And the 'Show Keys' checkbox with data-testid 'show-keys-checkbox' is checked
    When the user rapidly clicks the 'Show Keys' checkbox five times
    Then the final state of each piano key with data-testid starting with 'piano-key' should have the 'hide' class

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Display all piano keys with labels
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Display of Piano Keys
  The system must display all piano keys (white and black) in the UI, each labeled with its corresponding keyboard key.


  Scenario: [Normal] Display all piano keys with labels
    Given the Playable Piano webpage is loaded
    Then all piano keys should be visible
    And each piano key should display its corresponding keyboard key label
    And the labels should be 'a', 'w', 's', 'e', 'd', 'f', 't', 'g', 'y', 'h', 'u', 'j', 'k', 'o', 'l', 'p', ';'

reference_cases.title: [Normal] Playing a piano key using a mouse click
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Interacting with piano keys using mouse clicks and keyboard presses
  The system must allow the user to interact with the piano keys using both mouse clicks and keyboard presses, ensuring consistent functionality across both input methods.


Scenario: [Normal] Playing a piano key using a mouse click
    Given the webpage is loaded and the piano keys are visible
    When the user clicks on the white piano key with data-testid "piano-key-a"
    Then the audio should play
    And the piano key with data-testid "piano-key-a" should briefly have the "active" class applied
    And the "active" class should be removed after 150 milliseconds

reference_cases.title: [Error] Pressing a non-piano key on the keyboard
reference_cases.description:
Feature: Interacting with piano keys using mouse clicks and keyboard presses
  The system must allow the user to interact with the piano keys using both mouse clicks and keyboard presses, ensuring consistent functionality across both input methods.


  Scenario: [Error] Pressing a non-piano key on the keyboard
    Given the webpage is loaded and the piano keys are visible
    When the user presses the "z" key on the keyboard
    Then no audio file should play
    And no piano key should have the "active" class applied
